title: Three copies at the retention deadline
question: Original and export have expired retention; backup remains under a scoped hold. Which copies may be disposed of and which evidence establishes each disposition?
scenario: A customer case file exists as the system of record, an analyst export, and an encrypted backup. Retention expired for the original and export. A legal hold names the backup set containing the case. Operations must decide each copy’s custody and produce evidence before any medium is released or reused.
focalRelation: Data-lifecycle requirements become operational resource-protection and verifiable-disposal actions for each identified copy; one copy’s eligibility does not transfer to another copy with a different obligation.

nodes.label: System-of-record copy
nodes.detail: Retention expired, no hold applies, owner authorized disposition, and the copy remains in controlled storage until sanitation is verified.

nodes.label: Analyst export
nodes.detail: Retention expired and no hold applies, but the export must be located and its storage medium and replicas included in the disposition scope.

nodes.label: Backup copy
nodes.detail: A scoped legal hold applies, so operations must preserve and restrict this copy even though the ordinary retention period expired.

nodes.label: Execute and verify disposition
nodes.detail: For each authorized copy, choose a medium-appropriate method, verify execution, validate the result, and retain custody until acceptance.

nodes.label: Per-copy disposition record
nodes.detail: Record identity, authority, method, operator, verification result, exception or hold status, and final custody outcome for each copy.

edges.label: eligible after copy and replica scope is confirmed
hold blocks disposition for this copy
verified method and custody outcome become evidence

lanes.label: Persistent copy identities
lanes.rule: Keep original, export, and backup visible as concurrent copies with independent obligations.

lanes.label: Operational action and proof
lanes.rule: Disposition is complete only for the named copy after authorized execution, verification, validation, and recorded custody.

states.title: Three copies, three records
states.caption: Do not animate one record moving through locations; each copy exists concurrently and keeps its own scope.

states.title: The hold blocks only its scoped copy
states.caption: Original and export may proceed after authorization and scope confirmation. The backup remains preserved.

states.title: Execute without releasing custody
states.caption: Operations verifies and validates the selected method for the original and every located export replica.

states.title: Evidence closes only the eligible copies
states.caption: Disposition evidence records the original and export outcomes; the backup ledger records continued hold custody.

variants.label: Export replica discovered late
variants.changedFact: After the primary export is sanitized, an indexed replica is discovered in a collaboration workspace.

states.title: Disposition scope was incomplete
states.caption: The primary export’s evidence cannot establish disposition of a separately existing replica.

states.title: Authorize and verify the replica separately
states.caption: Apply the same lifecycle requirement to the newly identified copy and append its own disposition evidence.

nodes.label: Replica disposition path
nodes.detail: Authorize, sanitize, verify, and record the newly identified copy as its own subject.

states.title: Eligibility is not authorization

states.title: Authorize before executing the method
states.caption: After the owner approves the named copy and method, operations may sanitize, verify, validate, and record its outcome.

nodes.label: Approved sanitation method
nodes.detail: The method may execute only after owner authorization and scope confirmation for this medium.

nodes.label: Media-specific disposition evidence
nodes.detail: Record owner authority, method, verification, validation, and custody outcome for this copy.

prediction.prompt: Which copies may enter sanitization now?

options.label: All located copies, because retention expiry overrides the backup hold
options.feedback: A scoped preservation duty overrides ordinary disposition for the backup copy.

options.label: No copy, because the backup hold automatically extends to the entire case
options.feedback: The hold does not automatically expand to copies outside its scope. Evaluate and document each copy.

options.label: Original and located export, after owner authorization and scope confirmation
options.feedback: Correct. Their retention expired and no hold applies; the backup remains preserved under its scoped hold.

prediction.hint: Apply obligations to persistent copy identities rather than to an abstract record.

transfer.prompt: A collaboration-workspace replica appears after the export’s disposition record was signed. What follows?

options.label: Treat the replica as a still-existing copy and disposition it separately
options.feedback: Correct. Evidence for one copy cannot prove destruction of an omitted replica.

options.label: Treat the signed export record as proof for the later workspace replica
options.feedback: The evidence is bounded by its named scope, media, and verification result.

options.label: Preserve the replica automatically because the backup set has a scoped hold
options.feedback: A hold must be interpreted by its actual scope; neither inclusion nor exclusion should be invented.

transfer.hint: Ask which physical or logical copy the verification actually observed.

retry.prompt: A fourth removable-media copy has expired retention and no hold, but the data owner has not authorized disposition. What may operations do now?

options.label: Sanitize it because retention expiry is sufficient disposition authority
options.feedback: Expiry establishes eligibility for a decision path; it does not replace the required owner authorization and scope confirmation.

options.label: Keep custody, obtain owner authorization, then execute and verify the approved method
options.feedback: Correct. Eligibility, authorization, execution, verification, and evidence remain separate obligations for this copy.

options.label: Release it after an administrator records a successful delete operation
options.feedback: An administrator action does not substitute for owner authority, sanitization validation, or custody evidence.

retry.hint: Retention expiry makes the copy eligible for disposition; identify who must authorize the action before custody changes.

takeaway: Lifecycle rules become operational controls per copy. Holds, replicas, custody, sanitation, and disposition evidence remain scoped to the identified copy rather than inheriting another copy’s result.
assumptions: The hold’s scope explicitly includes the named backup and does not name the original or export.
The owner has authority to approve disposition of unheld copies.
The case does not prescribe a sanitation method without media and reuse facts.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The ledger keeps three copies concurrent, applies the lifecycle-to-resource-protection relationship to each scope, and requires copy-specific operational evidence.
